//: parts.json -- THE partition of Fizzygum's shipped source into a core plus named PARTS.
WHAT A PART IS. A named slice of the system that can be included or excluded as a unit, and
(from arc 4 phase 2) loaded at boot or on demand. Every directory that ships appears in
EXACTLY ONE part; a .coffee file under src/ that no part claims is a BUILD FAILURE
(buildSystem/check-shippable-coverage.js). That is stronger than what came before: build.py
used to carry a hand-maintained sequence of glob('src/<dir>/*.coffee') calls, and a new
directory that nobody remembered to add there shipped as NOTHING -- the build stayed green and
the only symptom was a runtime '<NewClass> is not defined'.
WHAT REPLACED WHAT (arc 4 phase 1). Part membership is what the whole-file marker
'# this file is excluded from the fizzygum homepage build' used to say, one file at a time, in
45 files, read by three regexes in build.py. Those are all gone. Exclusion is now a property of
a NAMED SLICE, stated once -- rather than an invisible property of a file you only discover by
opening it.
WHERE INCLUSION LIVES (arc 5): NOT here. A part is in an artifact because the PROFILE being
built names it -- buildSystem/profiles/<name>.json, read by buildSystem/buildProfile.py. This
file is the partition (what the parts ARE and what they own); a profile is the flavour (which of
them ship). The 'inHomepage' boolean that used to sit on each part below was inclusion for the
ONE hard-coded flavour, and it is gone: 'which parts does production have?' is answered by
reading profiles/homepage.json, not by grepping eleven booleans.
INCLUSION AND TIMING ARE DIFFERENT PROPERTIES (do not conflate them -- arc 4 reframe R6):
inclusion is a profile's business (above); `eager` here is TIMING -- loaded at boot, or on
demand? A marker could only ever express the first. Keeping them separate is what let arc 4
change inclusion with provably zero runtime change, leaving timing to its next phase.
FIELDS
dirs         directories whose *.coffee files belong to this part. Not recursive: list each.
eager        default true. false = loaded on demand (needs a launch site that awaits
world.parts.ensureLoaded, NOT a bare `if TheClass?` guard).
requires     other PARTS whose classes this part's code names. Two readers, one statement:
(1) buildProfile.py fails a profile that ships this part without them -- the
both-or-neither pairing that used to live only in prose, and whose absence
shipped a desktop icon whose click could only reject; (2) for a LAZY part,
PartsRegistry loads them FULLY FIRST, before ingesting this part's own batches
-- the only thing that makes `class X extends Y` across a part boundary safe,
since a door naming two parts goes through ensureAllLoaded = Promise.all and
orders nothing.
WARN It is NOT a licence for an EAGER part to name a LAZY part's class
unguarded: the eager part is already running at boot, so `requires` can only
promise the lazy one SHIPS, never that it has arrived. Those sites still guard
or await -- check-part-edges.js filters exactly those entries out (an
eager->EAGER requirement still counts: both are there from frame one). It did
NOT do so until 2026-08-02, when adding the app-kit edges turned it up: every
owner got its whole list, and that set is tested BEFORE the inheritance check,
so an eager part could even `extends` a lazy one's class with the build green.
STOP Cycles are rejected by build.py: a cycle has no valid ingest order.
requiresFlag optional build flag this part additionally needs, on TOP of being selected by the
profile. One carrier left ('videoPlayer'): a per-invocation opt-in rather than a
property of an artifact. ('tests' is gone -- whether the test machinery ships is
now just whether a profile selects the harness part, so it is not asked twice.)
bootPrelude  optional src/boot/*.coffee pieces concatenated into the boot bundle when this part
ships. Not part sources (those are classes, wrapped as text and compiled in the
browser): these are prototype extensions the bundle needs before any class runs.
numbertimes.coffee is the one carrier -- it extends Number for the fizzytiles LCL
preprocessor, and it used to be appended under `if ! $homepage`, i.e. the build
script knew a fact about a part.
vendor       optional non-source payloads that must arrive with the part, each
{ out: <path relative to the build root>, concat: [<pieces relative to
Fizzygum/>] }. build.py ASSEMBLES each one (pieces joined by a newline-semicolon
separator) for parts that ship, and emits only `out` into window.FIZZYGUM_PARTS,
because PartsRegistry consumes vendor entries as URLs to inject. Before arc 5
the fizzytiles payload was cat'd together by build_it_please.sh under `if the
vendored source file exists` -- no part or flavour test at all -- while its own
comment claimed 'emitted for every flavour that ships the part'. So a --homepage
tree carried 18.9 KB of software-3D engine for a part it does not ship.
assets       optional non-source FILES copied into the build tree for this part, as
[<path relative to Fizzygum/>, <destination dir relative to the build root>]
pairs. A part that does not ship copies none of them, which is how a flavour
stops shipping an asset with nobody maintaining a prune list. Arc 5 PR-D6:
the tail is DERIVED, never declared -- these pairs say who OWNS a file, and
what ships follows from that. The three pointer icons and FileSaver/JSZip used
to be copied unconditionally and then deleted again by the --homepage block.
So a part can own four kinds of thing -- sources (dirs), files (assets), assembled payloads
(vendor) and boot-bundle pieces (bootPrelude) -- and ALL FOUR appear or vanish together with the
part. That is the whole mechanism by which a flavour stops shipping something.
A part's absence must be a NO-OP at every call site, via the class-existence guard idiom
(`if DemoMenus?`, `world.pinouts?.reset()`, `WorldTestSupport.installOnto WorldWdgt if ...?`).
buildSystem/check-part-edges.js enforces that: an unguarded core reference to a part-owned
class fails the build.
CURRENT-STATE REFERENCE: docs/architecture/build-and-packaging.md -- the partition, the profiles,
and the full table of what a build DERIVES rather than declares. The arcs that produced this
shape: docs/archive/build-arc-4-dynamic-parts-plan.md (the partition) and
docs/archive/build-arc-5-packaging-profiles-plan.md (the profiles that select from it).

core.//: The product. Ships in every flavour, always eagerly. src/boot is absent on purpose: build_it_please.sh compiles those files BY NAME into the boot bundle, so they are not text-wrapped sources and not part material.
core.//two-that-stay: ⛔ CanvasWdgt (src/basic-widgets) and PatchNodeWdgt (src/patch-programming) STAY, and this is a decision rather than a residue. buildSystem/what-pins-core.js reports both as unreached from boot, so they look like 'app-kit' material -- and they are BLOCKED, by rule rather than by cost: the EAGER 'video-player' part extends CanvasWdgt (VideoPlayerCanvasWdgt, SimpleImageWdgt) and the EAGER 'patch-programming-experimental' part extends PatchNodeWdgt (DiffingPatchNodeWdgt, RegexSubstitutionPatchNodeWdgt), and an eager part cannot extend a LAZY part's class at all -- it is running from the first frame, so the base has to be DEFINED at boot and `requires` can only promise that a part ships, never that it arrived. Unblocking means making those two parts lazy. For 'video-player' that is not a packaging question at all: it is auto-launched AT BOOT (WorldWdgt: `if window.VideoPlayerWithRecommendationsWdgt? then world.draftRunVideoPlayer()`), so it would be a product decision about whether a flag-gated draft feature should launch itself. 'patch-programming-experimental' has no core entanglement left to point at -- nothing in core NAMES FanoutWdgt or FanoutPinWdgt in code any more (both survive only as prose, in WireSpec and ControllerMixin), and the one live construction site, DemoMenus, sits in the lazy 'demos' part, which already declares `requires: ["patch-programming-experimental"]`. What is left is a flag-less unfinished experiment that ships eagerly, so making it lazy is now a partition decision rather than a blocked one. 4.3 KB is not the reason to do either. ⚠ Independently of the blocker, CanvasWdgt is defensible core material on layering merits: it lives in src/basic-widgets and is the base three different parts' canvas widgets derive from -- 'no boot path reaches it' is not the same as 'it does not belong in core'.
core.//dataflow: ⚠ src/dataflow IS CORE, DELIBERATELY -- do not extract it (owner decision, 2026-07-30). It looks like an app slice next to src/spreadsheet, and it is not: it is the wiring substrate every widget reaches (ControllerMixin's wire verbs -- wireTo / trackTarget / declareWireTo -- mirror a controller's whole wire list into the engine through DataflowEngine.ensureWireEdges), and WorldWdgt.doOneCycle drains it EVERY cycle. Its absence is a no-op at NO call site, in either direction: a handful of reaches are optional-chained (`world.dataflow?.…` -- six today, in Widget's teardown and the spreadsheet), where a missing engine is silently ACCEPTED and that wire simply never fires; every other reach names it bare -- around thirty, thirteen of them in ControllerMixin alone, plus doOneCycle's own drain -- where the first cycle throws (recount with `grep -rn world.dataflow src`). Quietly dead or loudly fatal: wires never fire, sliders stop driving their targets, patch nodes go dead. That is broken, not reduced, and it fails the absence-must-be-a-no-op rule below. Same judgment as src/meta.
core.//assets: The boot splash + spinner (drawn before any class exists) and the CoffeeScript compiler, which ships in EVERY profile: FizzyPaint tools, spreadsheet formulas, $src snapshot records and Fizzytiles' LCL are all compiled at runtime, so a compiler-less build is a non-interactive kiosk (arc 5 PR-D3).

app-kit.//: THE SHARED BASE LAYER THE APP PARTS ARE BUILT FROM. Nine classes: the app protocol (WindowedApp, which owns `launch` and its requiredParts await), the toolbar/creator-button family (ToolbarWdgt, ToolbarCreatorButtonWdgt, CreatorButtonWdgt plus the two mixins they are made of -- ParentStainerMixin and WidgetCreatorAndSmartPlacerOnClickMixin), the tool-panel grid a toolbar lays its buttons out in (ToolPanelWdgt + its GlassBoxTopWdgt template header), and SpeechBubbleWdgt. 23.3 KB source, 9.8 KB code.
app-kit.//why-a-part-of-its-own: ⚠⚠ THEY ARE A LAYER, NOT A LEFTOVER -- and pricing them against the WRONG home is what made them look immovable for two arcs. Nothing at boot reaches any of them (buildSystem/what-pins-core.js reported exactly these, plus the two below, every run); they stayed in core only because two or more LAZY parts DERIVE from them, and before `requires` a cross-part base class was an unordered race with nowhere safe to put it. `fg whatpins` proposes 'authoring' as their home, because that is the part that NAMES them most -- and priced that way every one is a bad trade: 'plots' and 'maps' would each have to declare `requires: ["authoring"]`, so opening a chart or a map would first fetch and compile 225.5 KB of Makers it does not use. But they are not authoring's classes: `fg hypopart` counts 44 inheritance edges from 9 parts (11 parts declare `requires: ["app-kit"]` -- 'demos' and 'dev-tools' merely NAME a class here rather than deriving from one), which is the definition of a shared base. They are the layer 'authoring' ITSELF derives from. So the home is a part of their own that every consumer requires, and the toll drops from 225.5 KB to 23.3 KB of material the consumer is actually built out of.
app-kit.//eager: LAZY, and it costs a consumer nothing extra: every part that derives from it is lazy too and declares `requires` on this one, so PartsRegistry brings this part FULLY IN before ingesting the consumer's own batches -- the only construct that orders a cross-part `class X extends Y` (ensureAllLoaded is a Promise.all and orders nothing). ⚠ The one EAGER namer left is dev-tools' WidgetFactory.createNewSpeechBubbleWdgt, and it AWAITS rather than guarding, exactly like its two demo-part siblings in the same file: a guard answers 'is it here?' when the question is 'get it here', and on a lazy part it would silently swallow the menu click.
app-kit.//stays-in-core: ⛔ CanvasWdgt and PatchNodeWdgt are reported alongside these nine by `fg whatpins` and deliberately do NOT come -- see the '//two-that-stay' note on 'core' above for the pricing.

meta-tools.//: The in-world INSPECTORS: InspectorWdgt, ClassInspectorWdgt (its subclass) and ConsoleWdgt. Split out of src/meta so that a lean/appliance profile can leave them out -- src/meta itself CANNOT become a part, because Class and Mixin live there and are the compile bootstrap. Production ships it (profiles/homepage.json names it) and always has; the `lean` profile is what drops it outright. Core reaches it through exactly two sites, Widget.spawnInspector and Widget.createConsole.
meta-tools.//eager: LAZY. An inspector is the definition of on-demand: nobody opens one during a normal session, and on a precompiled tree a lazy part's classes are absent from js/pre-compiled.js, so production stops paying for them up front. It pairs naturally with sources: "lazy" -- opening an inspector ALREADY had to await the reflective layer (an inspector reads class member maps, which exist only once the source text is ingested), so the part load joins an await that was there anyway. ⚠ The two call sites must NOT use `if InspectorWdgt?`: for a lazy part that reads 'not fetched yet' and swallows the click forever. They ask world.parts.isAvailable (did this artifact ship it at all) and then await.

fizzytiles.//: The Fizzytiles ('fridge magnets') engine: the tile widgets, the LiveCodeLang compiler/preprocessor/runner, and the SW3D output pane. THE LAZY PART -- the largest self-contained app in the tree, with a vendored 3D payload, reached from exactly two entry points. Its door FridgeMagnetsApp is in here too: the desktop icon is built at boot from core art plus a class NAME, so nothing of the app is needed until that icon is clicked. 'eager: false' means index.html does not carry it until someone launches it; the harness and index-sw.html override that (FIZZYGUM_EAGER_ALL_PARTS) because a part arriving mid-test would be frame-paced and therefore cycle-count-dependent.
fizzytiles.//requires: ⛔ MANDATORY (inheritance): its door, FridgeMagnetsApp, extends WindowedApp, which is in 'app-kit'. ⚠ This is NOT the door naming its own app parts (the thing the 'example-*' notes below forbid) -- it is the base class the door is DEFINED from, which has to be ingested before this part's classes exist at all.
fizzytiles.//bootPrelude: Number::times / ::timesWithVariable, which the LiveCodeLang preprocessor emits for `3 times with i box`. It extends a built-in prototype, so it belongs in the boot bundle rather than among the part's classes -- but it exists ONLY for this part, and used to be appended by build_it_please.sh under `if ! $homepage`: a fact about a part, kept in the build script.

vendor.//: SWCanvas's subtractive 3D-CORE dist target (Surface + DepthBuffer + Texture3D + Triangle3DOps, ~14 KB vs ~263 KB for the full engine, pixel-identical on the 3D path) plus the minified SW3D userland engine. ⚠ The SW pages must NOT load this: their boot bundle carries the FULL SWCanvas as their renderer, so injecting the subtractive build over it would replace a superset with a subset. PartsRegistry's vendor step is idempotent and skips it when window.SW3D and SWCanvas.Core.Triangle3DOps are already present.

demos.//: The demo/parts-bin catalogue (DemoMenus, reached as `demoMenus`) and the sample widgets it shows off: the bouncer, the pen, the pointer. Arc 3 extracted DemoMenus out of MenusHelper for exactly this; its own header already said 'arc 4 turns that into part membership'.
demos.//eager: LAZY. Nothing reaches the demo family until someone opens the 'demo ➜' or 'test menu ➜' entries, so it has no business compiling at boot -- 28 classes with src/demos-icons folded in. ⚠ Its doors are MENU ITEMS, which makes them a shape the app launchers do not have: a menu is BUILT synchronously (ButtonWdgt binds `@target[@action]` at build time), so the item cannot target the `demoMenus` singleton -- core owns the item, asks `world.parts.isAvailable "demos"` to decide whether to OFFER it, and awaits inside the action. See Widget.popUpDemoTestMenu. ⚠ Not shipped by any production profile, so this buys dev-page boot and partition uniformity, never download size.
demos.//icons: src/demos-icons holds the 23 icon classes ONLY DemoMenus names -- text-formatting glyphs (align/bold/italic/font-size/format-as-code), the collapsed/uncollapsed state pair, the little USA/world map glyphs, and the welcome/templates/text/video-play/C-F icons. They sat in src/icons, which is otherwise product, and are here for the same reason src/icons-dev exists: an icon belongs to whatever names it. ⚠ Their *IconAppearance siblings live ELSEWHERE, and not in core: 13 are named by toolbar buttons that 'authoring' took, so 11 sit in src/authoring-icons and the little-map 2 in src/maps, reached across a part boundary that `requires` orders. Only the five appearances whose sole namer was their own moving widget travelled into this directory.
demos.//requires: The demo catalogue SHOWS OFF other parts: the icon gallery (dev-icons) and the unfinished patch nodes (patch-programming-experimental), both EAGER, so for those two this is purely an INCLUSION statement -- a profile with 'demos' must carry them or those menu entries would throw on click. 'authoring' (which also holds the Maker apps this opens by name), 'maps' and 'examples-icons' are LAZY, so for those three it is also an ORDERING statement -- and for 'examples-icons' the ordering is MANDATORY rather than convenient, because CFDegreesConverterIconAppearance EXTENDS a class in it and a base class arriving concurrently is a race, not a catchable error, and PartsRegistry brings them in fully before any demo class exists.
demos.//requires-why-lazy-two: ⚠ THE LAZY TWO ARE FORCED, not a preference. 14 of src/demos-icons' widgets reach their *IconAppearance through `createAppearance: -> new FooIconAppearance @` -- 12 in 'authoring' (the text-formatting glyphs plus templates/video-play), 2 in 'maps' (the little USA/world glyphs) -- and CreatorButtonWdgt's constructor does `@appearance = @createAppearance()`, consuming the value synchronously. There is no seam to await through, which is the same no-async-seam rule that governs creator buttons, so a per-site await cannot exist at those 14 sites and `requires` is the only shape available. (DemoMenus' own references COULD each await; they ride along on this declaration rather than being hand-written 30-odd times.) ⚠ 'plots' is deliberately NOT here for exactly the contrast: every reference to it sits in a menu action with a real seam, so those await per site and a demo menu does not drag the charting part in.
demos.//requires-app-kit: 'app-kit' is the shared base layer, and DemoMenus.createToolsPanel builds one of its widgets (`new ScrollPanelWdgt new ToolPanelWdgt`). That one site is a menu action and could have awaited per-site -- the finer instrument, and what 'plots' gets -- but it would buy nothing here: this part already requires 'authoring', which requires 'app-kit', so the base layer is in before a single demo class is ingested no matter what. Declaring it states the fact once instead of encoding the same dependency in a second idiom, and it keeps check-part-edges.js reading one level rather than chasing a chain.

authoring.//: THE AUTHORING SURFACE: the six framed content citizens a user composes documents in -- GenericPanelWdgt and its DashboardWdgt / SlideWdgt / ImageWdgt (Draw) / PatchProgrammingWdgt subclasses, plus DocumentWdgt (Docs Maker) and the WelcomeMessageInfoWdgt built on it -- together with every tool palette that serves them and the creator buttons those palettes hold. Around 140 sources across the part's two dirs -- the authoring classes themselves in src/authoring, plus the icon appearances and their icon widgets in src/authoring-icons, which only these buttons name. Both dirs grow: count them rather than quoting a number.
authoring.//eager: LAZY. Nothing here exists until a desktop icon is clicked: each of the eight launcher apps here awaits at its `launch`, exactly as SpreadsheetApp does. Production ships it (profiles/homepage.json names it), so a visitor who never opens a Maker never downloads one -- and unlike 'demos' this part is in `lean` too, which makes it the first slice since the spreadsheet to cut the PRODUCTION image rather than only dev boot.
authoring.//why-one-part: ⚠⚠ IT IS ONE PART BECAUSE INHERITANCE SAYS SO, not because that was the tidiest carve. DashboardWdgt / SlideWdgt / ImageWdgt / PatchProgrammingWdgt all `extends GenericPanelWdgt`, and WelcomeMessageInfoWdgt `extends DocumentWdgt`. A door may name SEVERAL parts (`whenAllLoaded ["maps", "plots"]`), which is enough for a REFERENCE -- but not for a base class: ensureAllLoaded is a Promise.all, so two parts named at one door load CONCURRENTLY with no ordering between them, and `class X extends Y` across that boundary is a race. Within one part _ingestPartPromise orders by findLoadOrder(). So an inheritance family is indivisible: splitting this per app or per toolbar is not a smaller version of this part, it is a broken one.
authoring.//toolbars: ⚠ A TOOLBAR CANNOT LEAVE WITHOUT ITS HOST. Each palette's docked home reaches it through the synchronous `buildToolbar` hook (DocumentWdgt -> TextToolbarWdgt, SlideWdgt -> SlidesToolbarWdgt, DashboardWdgt -> DashboardsToolbarWdgt, PatchProgrammingWdgt -> its own, ImageWdgt -> PaintToolbarWdgt), a pure factory with no seam to await through -- so host and palette travel together. The floating homes are ToolbarCreatorButtonWdgt subclasses, which are creator buttons and cannot await either; they are here for the reason the maps/plots buttons are in their parts.
authoring.//stays-in-core: Four groups did NOT come, each for a stated reason. ⚠ THE FIRST OF THEM HAS SINCE MOVED, and reading why is worth more than the entry: ToolbarWdgt, CreatorButtonWdgt and ToolbarCreatorButtonWdgt stayed because the LAZY 'plots' part extends all three, so putting them HERE would have made 'plots' declare `requires: ["authoring"]` and fetch 225.5 KB of Makers to open a chart. That was the right verdict about THIS home and the wrong one about the classes: they are the base layer 'authoring' itself derives from, so they now live in 'app-kit' with their two mixins, which 'plots', 'maps' and this part all require for 23.3 KB. The three groups below still hold. The eight window-chrome buttons (Close/Collapse/Uncollapse/Edit/IconButtonWdgt/UpperRightTriangleIconicButtonWdgt/ExternalLinkButtonWdgt/VideoPlayButtonWdgt): FrameBarWdgt builds them on every window and EditableMarkWdgt extends one. PatchNodeWdgt + CalculatingPatchNodeWdgt: the EAGER 'patch-programming-experimental' part extends them, so they must be defined at boot. And 107 of the 118 remaining src/icons files, which are named by something that stays -- mostly DemoMenus.
authoring.//doors: Eight of the desktop's nine icon apps LIVE here now (their icons are built at boot from core art plus a class NAME, so nothing of them is needed until clicked). They await here (SimpleDocumentApp, SimpleSlideApp, DashboardsApp, FizzyPaintApp, GenericPanelApp, PatchProgrammingApp, ToolbarsApp, HowToSaveMessageApp), plus InfoDocs.createNextTo, which builds every app's info window out of a DocumentWdgt. The ninth desktop opener, FridgeMagnetsApp, sits in 'fizzytiles' -- the part it opens -- which is the door shape again rather than an exception; DegreesConverterApp likewise left for its own one-class 'example-degrees-converter' door in the Examples folder. ⚠ OTHER PARTS REACH IN: the four document doors in the `example-*` parts (SampleDocApp / SampleSlideApp / SampleDashboardApp / DegreesConverterApp each ASSEMBLE one of these citizens -- REQUIRED, so each declares it in `requiredParts` and the inherited `launch` awaits it) and 'demos' (DemoMenus builds an ImageWdgt, a SlideWdgt, a DocumentWdgt and the WelcomeMessageInfoWdgt, covered by `demos requires [authoring]`). Both pairings ARE verified now -- check-part-edges.js covers every source present at boot plus each lazy part.
authoring.//requires: ⛔ MANDATORY, and it is INHERITANCE that makes it so. 30 classes here derive from 'app-kit' -- every Maker app from WindowedApp, every docked palette from ToolbarWdgt, every floating palette opener from ToolbarCreatorButtonWdgt, every tool button from CreatorButtonWdgt, and EditorContentPropertyChangerButtonWdgt mixes in ParentStainerMixin. A base class arriving concurrently is a race rather than a catchable error, so only `requires` (PartsRegistry loads it FULLY FIRST) makes this legal; a per-site await could not exist at a `class X extends Y` line at all.

plots.//: The plots/graphs family: AxisWdgt, PlotWithAxesWdgt, the four Example*Plot widgets and the 3D plot's little geometry kit (Point3D, Grid3D, PlaneGrid3D), plus the four creator buttons that make them, the PlotsToolbarWdgt palette and the button that pops it. 12 KB of code and ~19 KB of 3D scaffolding, none of it reachable until someone asks for a chart.
plots.//eager: LAZY, for the same reason as maps: production ships it (the sample dashboard, the sample slide and the sample doc all BUILD plots, so it cannot be dropped) but a lazy part's classes are absent from js/pre-compiled.js, so the first load does not carry it.
plots.//buttons: ⚠ The four creator buttons AND PlotsToolbarWdgt/PlotsToolbarCreatorButtonWdgt live here, not in core, and for two different reasons. The buttons: a creator button has no async seam (see the maps part), so it must sit in the part it creates from. The TOOLBAR: every one of its four items is a plot button, so a core toolbar filtering them out would open an EMPTY palette window -- worse than not offering it. Keeping the palette and its opener in the part means SuperToolbarWdgt filters ONE button and the palette is simply not offered until plots is in.
plots.//requires: ⛔ MANDATORY (inheritance): the four plot creator buttons extend CreatorButtonWdgt, PlotsToolbarWdgt extends ToolbarWdgt and PlotsToolbarCreatorButtonWdgt extends ToolbarCreatorButtonWdgt -- all in 'app-kit'. ⚠ This is the edge that used to be the argument for leaving those three base classes in core: naming 'authoring' (their old proposed home) would have meant fetching 225.5 KB of Makers to open a chart. Against the base layer's own part it is 23.3 KB of material every one of these classes is literally built from, which is why the objection went away rather than being accepted.

maps.//: The two vector maps -- SimpleUSAMapIconWdgt and SimpleWorldMapIconWdgt, each with its *Appearance -- and the two toolbar buttons that create them. 4 files but ~85 KB: the appearances are long vector-path artwork, which makes this the best bytes-per-edge slice in the tree and the least likely to be missed by a user who never opens it.
maps.//eager: LAZY, and production ships it that way: a lazy part's classes are NOT in js/pre-compiled.js (the image is harvested by booting index.html, where lazy parts by definition do not load), so profiles/homepage.json can keep the Examples AND not download the artwork until someone asks for a map.
maps.//buttons: ⚠ WHY THE TWO CREATOR BUTTONS LIVE HERE rather than with the other sample content. A creator button has NO async seam -- WidgetCreatorAndSmartPlacerOnClickMixin.activated and Widget.grabbedWidgetSwitcheroo both consume createWidgetToBeHandled()'s RETURN VALUE synchronously -- so a button outside this part could not await the load before constructing a map. Keeping the button in the part it creates from makes its mere EXISTENCE proof that its part is loaded, which is what turns an `if USAMapCreatorButtonWdgt?` filter in the core toolbars into a correct test instead of a swallowed click.
maps.//requires: ⛔ MANDATORY (inheritance): USAMapCreatorButtonWdgt and WorldMapCreatorButtonWdgt both extend CreatorButtonWdgt, which is in 'app-kit'. The note above says a creator button must live in the part it creates FROM; this is the other half of that -- it must also be ORDERED after the part it is built OUT OF.

examples-icons.//: The icon ART that ONLY the Examples folder draws -- today the C-F converter glyph (DegreesConverterIconWdgt and its 9.5 KB appearance). It is here and not in core because nothing else needs it: the folder's other four icons (typewriter, slide, dashboards, the generic shortcut frame) are drawn by DESKTOP icons and by FolderWindowWdgt/BinOpenerWdgt at boot, so they stay core and could not move even if this part wanted them.
examples-icons.//eager: LAZY, fetched when the Examples FOLDER IS OPENED -- the middle tier of three. Boot draws no folder contents at all (ExamplesFolderWindowWdgt starts empty); opening it fetches this art and builds the five icons; clicking one fetches THAT app. ⇒ an icon costs its art on open and its app on click, and a visitor who never opens the folder pays for neither.

example-degrees-converter.//: ONE DOOR OF THE DESKTOP'S 'Examples' FOLDER, ALONE IN ITS PART -- and the part is one class because the LOADING UNIT IS THE PART: five doors in one part would mean opening any of them fetched all five. DegreesConverterApp -- the C/F converter built out of patch-programming nodes.
example-degrees-converter.//eager: ⚠⚠ NOTHING FETCHES THIS UNTIL ITS ICON IS CLICKED. The folder's icons are built at boot from CORE art by WorldWdgt.createDesktop, and the launcher holds the app's class NAME rather than a live app object (AppLauncherWdgt's lazy mode), so drawing the Examples folder costs no part at all. On the click the launcher asks PartsRegistry which part owns that name, loads it, and launches -- so this file's source is fetched, compiled and run at that moment and not one instant sooner. ⇒ a launcher does NOT have to be eager; only something reached at BOOT does, and an icon's ART is not its app. ⛔ NO parts.json `requires` on the APP PARTS here, deliberately: on a lazy part `requires` also ORDERS the load (requirements fully first), so naming them would drag the app in behind the door instead of behind the click. The class declares its own `requiredParts`, which its inherited `launch` awaits and buildProfile.py checks for shipping. ⚠⚠ THE `requires: ["app-kit"]` BELOW DOES NOT REVERSE THAT -- it is the opposite case, and the distinction is what the two mechanisms can each reach. `requiredParts` is awaited INSIDE `launch`, which is long after this class had to be DEFINED; 'app-kit' holds WindowedApp, which this door EXTENDS, so it has to be ingested before the door exists at all and `requires` is the only construct that orders that. The prohibition is about what a door DRAGS IN behind itself; this is what the door is MADE OF.
example-degrees-converter.//requires: Its buildIcon names DegreesConverterIconWdgt, which is the 'examples-icons' part. In the normal flow that art is already in (the folder had to be OPENED to reach this icon), but a SNAPSHOT can pull this app in with no folder ever opened -- Serializer.classNamesIn walks {'$wk':'app:...'} keys -- so the dependency is declared rather than assumed. Ordering it costs nothing: the art is 2 files and, on the path that matters, already resident. 'app-kit' is the other kind of entry entirely -- see the ⚠⚠ above: DegreesConverterApp EXTENDS WindowedApp, so that part is not a dependency this door reaches for, it is what the door is compiled against.

spreadsheet.//: The spreadsheet ENGINE: the grid (SimpleSpreadsheetWdgt), its frame, the widgetised cells and headers with their appearances, the sparse SheetModel + SheetCellRecord, FormulaCompiler/FormulaHelpers and SheetError. 13 files, ~114 KB -- the largest app-like slice that was still sitting inside core. Its door, SpreadsheetApp, is alone in the LAZY 'example-sheet' part: its Examples-folder icon is built at boot from a class NAME and core art, so this engine needs no eager sliver to put an icon on screen, and the door's own source arrives only when that icon is clicked.
spreadsheet.//eager: LAZY, and production ships it that way (profiles/homepage.json names it): a lazy part's classes are absent from js/pre-compiled.js, so a visitor who never opens a sheet never pays for one. The one door is SpreadsheetApp.launch, which awaits.
spreadsheet.//dataflow: ⚠ THE ENGINE IT DEPENDS ON IS NOT HERE, ON PURPOSE. Cells are dataflow nodes, but src/dataflow stays in CORE -- it is the wiring substrate the whole system uses (ControllerMixin's wire verbs, mirrored into the engine by DataflowEngine.ensureWireEdges -- sliders, patch nodes, and WorldWdgt.doOneCycle's every-cycle drain), not an app slice, and its absence would be a semantic break rather than a no-op: silent at the handful of optional-chained reaches, a first-cycle throw at the bare ones (see the 'core' part's //dataflow note above). So the dependency is stated the other way round: SpreadsheetApp -- the door, alone in 'example-sheet' -- names this ONE part in its own `requiredParts`, which its inherited `launch` awaits. A parts.json `requires` would be the opposite construct: what a part is MADE OF, ingested before its classes exist. See docs/archive/core-app-slices-partition-plan.md §4 Phase 3 (amended) for the enumeration that settled it.

dev-tools.//: In-world dev scaffolding: the widget factory (world.widgetFactory) and the pinout debug overlay (world.pinouts, an arc-3 extraction). Both are already optional collaborators behind an existence guard. (The layout-editing chrome the factory instantiates lives in 'authoring' -- see //requires.)
dev-tools.//requires: WidgetFactory builds the bouncer and the pen, which are demo widgets, a speech bubble, which is 'app-kit', and the layout adder/droplet + the test-screen layout gallery, which are 'authoring'. Its factory methods AWAIT those parts (timing); this line is the other half (inclusion) -- on a profile with dev-tools but no demos / no app-kit / no authoring those awaits could only reject. ⚠⚠ THE AWAIT IS WHAT ACTUALLY PROTECTS THE SITE, and this declaration must never be read as replacing it: this part is EAGER, so `requires` can promise the other part SHIPS but never that it has ARRIVED. All requirements here are LAZY, so check-part-edges.js discounts this line entirely when scanning these files -- drop an await and the build fails, which is the intended reading.

dev-icons.//: The icon gallery the demo menus show: chapter markers, information, raster-pic, save, under-carpet. Moved out of the 159-file src/icons, which is otherwise all product.

patch-programming-experimental.//: The unfinished half of patch programming: fanout, diffing, regex-substitution nodes. src/patch-programming was a MIXED directory (PatchNodeWdgt and CalculatingPatchNodeWdgt ship, these six do not) and P-D2 resolves a mixed directory by MOVING files, never by tagging them.

macros.//: The macro engine + toolkit (world.macroToolkit): the authoring path for SystemTests. Test machinery that lives in src/ because the macros drive the product through its own API. Was excluded by the FILE_ONLY_FOR_MACROS marker regex; now by part.

harness.//: The Automator + test-harness sources, which live in the SIBLING TESTS REPO. Its five *TestSupport classes install themselves onto core prototypes at boot behind `if XTestSupport?`. ⚠ THIS PART IS WHAT MAKES A BUILD TEST-CAPABLE, so five derived facts key off its presence (buildProfile.py): the js/tests symlink, BUILDFLAG_LOAD_TESTS, the two tests-repo build gates, and -- inverted -- the strip of the dead `if Automator?` branches, since Automator/AutomatorLoader/AutomatorPlayer are all in here. It used to carry `requiresFlag: "tests"` on top of a flavour test, which asked the same question twice.
harness.//requires: AutomatorEventCommandStartMacro builds its macros with Macro.fromString, so a test-capable build that somehow omitted 'macros' would carry a harness that cannot replay a single test. Both eager, so this is inclusion only.
harness.//assets: The three pointer icons SystemTestsControlPanelUpdater sets as in the harness control panel (DOM, not canvas -- so no screenshot gate can see them go missing; the parts fingerprint is what checks them), plus FileSaver + JSZip, which globalFunctions only loads when BUILDFLAG_LOAD_TESTS is set and which product FileSaving.coffee explicitly does not depend on.
